current_answer: People have built games, browser demos, desktop apps, art, brain engines and research tests on real fruit fly connectomes, mainly FlyWire (female brain) and MaleCNS (male brain and nerve cord). We checked 73 of them on 28 September 2026: 30 can be opened in a browser or free notebook without installing anything. Most viral demos really run a simulated fly brain, but a person chose which neurons receive the input and which neurons act, and several get most of their movement from scripts or trained parts; the Half-Life demo does not load a connectome at all by default. No fly has been "uploaded", and the three most-watched demo videos (Beat Saber, Bad Apple and NeuroCraft) are the ones we could verify least. Where studies use shuffled-wiring controls, the real wiring matters for fly reflexes but has not helped general machine-learning tasks, and a third-party test found that a brainless constant autopilot survives in Doom about as long as the viral full-brain fly (51.9 s vs 53.3 s). A beginner can run the published whole-brain model on a CPU: in our test on 2 CPUs (Linux, 28 minutes) sugar input drove the feeding motor neuron to 85.2 Hz, and shuffled wiring dropped it to 0 Hz.

catalogue_card.question: What have people built with the digital fruit fly brain, and what is real?
catalogue_card.text: 73 fruit fly brain simulation projects checked in code: 30 you can try online, 44 demo and lab videos with evidence grades, a Doom control test and seven connectome datasets compared.

summary: 73 entries checked on 28 Sep 2026 (15 new in the second check): 17 grade A, 13 B, 15 C, 3 D, 5 U and 20 datasets or tools (not graded).

Doom: in a third-party control study using DOOMFLY's own code, a brainless constant autopilot survived 51.9 s against 53.3 s for the full MaleCNS brain; shuffled wiring 6.7 s. The autopilot copies the fly's average output, so a constant policy reproduces the behaviour; this does not show the brain does nothing. DOOMFLY stays grade B.
30 entries have a no-install link; all answered our HTTP check, but none was played by us.

In viral demos a real connectome usually runs, but people chose the input and output neurons; DesktopFly, FlyCraft, Bad Apple, FlyDrones and the FlyBridge Minecraft farming demo get much of their visible behaviour from scripts, stimulus, training or a synthetic network, and the Half-Life demo (grade D) builds a synthetic network by default although its video claims MaleCNS v1.0.
Beat Saber, NeuroCraft and Eon's embodied fly have no inspectable code (grade U).

Video gallery (28 Sep 2026): 44 videos, 39 of them original uploads by the project's author, lab or institution; 26 of 73 catalogue entries have at least one video. Each card shows the project's grade from the catalogue and what the video does not show.
The most-watched demo clips are the least checkable: Beat Saber (about 23 million views) and NeuroCraft are grade U, and Bad Apple is grade C because its picture is mostly the stimulus.
"91%" is the share of 164 testable predictions of the brain-only Shiu et al. 2024 model that matched experiments; "95%" compares versions of the model and is not an accuracy.

Controlled studies (18): shuffled wiring abolishes fly reflexes (for example MN9 0 Hz vs 67.30 Hz), but fly wiring did no better than random or shuffled wiring on reservoir, language-model, hashing and trained Doom tasks (authors' numbers).
FlyWire data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); MaleCNS, MANC, hemibrain and BANC data are CC BY.

Build your own, tested 28 Sep 2026 on Linux with 2 CPUs and no GPU: the Shiu et al. model on FlyWire v783 gave MN9 85.2 ± 3.2 Hz with sugar input at 150 Hz, 0 Hz without input, and 0 Hz in 6 of 6 trials with shuffled wiring; 6 of 6 tests passed. Project pages now cover the Shiu et al. model and DOOMFLY.
uncertainty: No demo was played in a real browser; "page responds" is an HTTP check only.

Control and benchmark numbers are the authors' own (a third party's for doom-fly-control); we re-computed only one statistic (larva vs shuffles). Several new controls are small: one training seed, 4 runs per shuffle seed, 2 races.

Borderline grades: Fly Worker, fly-brain by Lulzx, The Fly's Hash Function, Fly OCR, Fly Self Driving (headline numbers only in its results document; stored JSON does not match) and the null-model study (brain compressed to 512 groups) are borderline A; fly-brain by erojas and Kick the Fly could argue B.
The five C grades added on 28 Sep 2026 rest on file citations that we spot-read but did not re-verify line by line.

The second check came only about 22 hours after the first, so "no changes" says little about how fast the field moves. Stars, creation and last-push dates of the 58 older entries were reused from 27 Sep 2026 and are labelled.
Why the Shiu v783 file has 616 fewer neurons than the FlyWire v783 release is not established; the scope of BANC's "approximately 188,000 neurons" is not stated.
The Beat Saber explanation and the MICrONS figures rest on search summaries only.

Not yet triaged: fly-connectome-template (graded, held back by the 15-entry limit), about 125 low-star GitHub leads and 211 repositories listed only in project directories. X and TikTok were not searched for new videos.
The Build your own guide is untested on macOS, Windows/WSL, Colab and machines with a C++ compiler; GitHub Pages publishing is untested. DOOMFLY's run steps are untested by us.
FlyWire data licence conflict: CC BY-NC 4.0 in the official guidelines vs CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo v783 record; we follow the stricter, non-commercial reading.

Video summaries rest on titles, descriptions, captions, code and thumbnails; we did not watch every video frame by frame. View counts are snapshots from 28 Sep 2026. The Half-Life video's uploader is matched to the code's author by name only.

Videos cannot play inside the site: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players failed in the site's sandboxed frames (tested in headless Chromium only; Safari, Firefox and mobile untested). YouTube and X thumbnails are loaded from their image servers.
